1.name: Segmentation
1.description: Divide an object or system into independent parts; make it sectional; increase the degree of fragmentation.

2.name: Taking out (Extraction)
2.description: Separate an interfering part or property from an object; extract only the necessary part or property.

3.name: Local quality
3.description: Transition from a homogeneous structure to a heterogeneous one; make each part function in conditions most suitable for its operation.

4.name: Asymmetry
4.description: Transition from symmetrical to asymmetrical forms; if an object is asymmetrical, increase its degree of asymmetry.

5.name: Merging
5.description: Bring closer in space the same or similar objects or operations; assemble identical or similar parts for parallel operations.

6.name: Universality
6.description: Make a part or object perform multiple functions; eliminate the need for other parts.

7.name: Nested doll (Nesting)
7.description: Place one object inside another; pass one object through a cavity in another.

8.name: Anti-weight (Counterweight)
8.description: To compensate for the weight of an object, merge it with other objects that provide lifting force.

9.name: Preliminary anti-action
9.description: If it is known that an object will experience harmful stress, apply counter-stress in advance.

10.name: Preliminary action
10.description: Perform, before it is needed, the required change of an object; pre-arrange objects so they can come into action from the most convenient position.

11.name: Beforehand cushioning
11.description: Prepare emergency means in advance to compensate for the relatively low reliability of an object.

12.name: Equipotentiality
12.description: Change the operating condition so that an object need not be raised or lowered.

13.name: The other way round (Inversion)
13.description: Invert the action used to solve the problem; make movable parts fixed, and fixed parts movable.

14.name: Spheroidality - Curvature
14.description: Move from flat surfaces to spherical ones; from linear to rotary motion; use rollers, balls, spirals.

15.name: Dynamics
15.description: Allow the characteristics of an object to change to be optimal at each stage of operation; divide into parts capable of moving.

16.name: Partial or excessive actions
16.description: If 100% of an objective is hard to achieve, use slightly less or more.

17.name: Another dimension
17.description: Move an object in two or three-dimensional space; use multi-layered arrangement.

18.name: Mechanical vibration
18.description: Cause an object to oscillate or vibrate; increase its frequency; use piezoelectric effect.

19.name: Periodic action
19.description: Replace a continuous action with a periodic (pulse) one; if an action is already periodic, change the frequency.

20.name: Continuity of useful action
20.description: Carry on work continuously; make all parts of an object work at full load all the time.

21.name: Skipping (Rushing through)
21.description: Conduct a process, or certain stages, at high speed.

22.name: Blessing in disguise
22.description: Use harmful factors to obtain a positive effect; eliminate the harmful by combining it with other harmful factors.

23.name: Feedback
23.description: Introduce feedback to improve a process or action; if feedback already exists, change its magnitude or influence.

24.name: Intermediary
24.description: Use an intermediate object to carry, transfer or transmit an action.

25.name: Self-service
25.description: Make an object serve itself by performing auxiliary and repair functions; use waste resources and energy.

26.name: Copying
26.description: Instead of an unavailable or expensive object, use simpler, inexpensive copies; replace a physical object with optical copies.

27.name: Cheap short-living objects
27.description: Replace an inexpensive object with an expensive one, sacrificing certain qualities.

28.name: Mechanics substitution
28.description: Replace a mechanical system with optical, acoustic, thermal or olfactory systems.

29.name: Pneumatics and hydraulics
29.description: Use gas and liquid parts instead of solid parts of an object.

30.name: Flexible shells and thin films
30.description: Use flexible shells and thin films instead of 3D structures; isolate objects using flexible shells.

31.name: Porous materials
31.description: Make an object porous or use supplementary porous elements; if already porous, fill pores with a substance.

32.name: Color changes
32.description: Change the color of an object or its environment; change the transparency of an object.

33.name: Homogeneity
33.description: Make objects interacting with the main object from the same material (or material with identical properties).

34.name: Discarding and recovering
34.description: Make portions of an object that have fulfilled their functions disappear or restore them directly in operation.

35.name: Parameter changes
35.description: Change an object's physical state; change the concentration or flexibility; change the temperature.

36.name: Phase transitions
36.description: Use phenomena occurring during phase transitions such as volume changes and heat absorption/liberation.

37.name: Thermal expansion
37.description: Use thermal expansion or contraction of materials; use materials with different coefficients of thermal expansion.

38.name: Strong oxidants
38.description: Replace ordinary air with oxygen-enriched air; replace enriched air with pure oxygen.

39.name: Inert atmosphere
39.description: Replace a normal environment with an inert one; carry out the process in a vacuum.

40.name: Composite materials
40.description: Transition from homogeneous to composite (multiple) materials.

1.name: Basic Principles & Simple Improvements
1.description: Focuses on simple improvements within the same field. Represents ~32% of innovations.

function_analysis.name: Function Analysis (FA)
function_analysis.description: Identify components, their functions, and associated costs. Maps useful and harmful interactions between system components.

ceca.name: Cause-Effect Chain Analysis (CECA)
ceca.description: Find root causes of problems by tracing cause-effect relationships. Reveals hidden causes behind undesired effects.

trimming.name: Trimming
trimming.description: Simplify the system by removing components while maintaining functions using remaining parts.

resources.name: Resources Identification
resources.description: Identify and utilize existing resources (space, time, substance, energy) within and around the system.

nine_windows.name: 9 Windows (System Operator)
nine_windows.description: Analyze the system across time (past, present, future) and scale (subsystem, system, supersystem).

2.name: Engineering Contradictions
2.description: Solves technical contradictions using established techniques from similar industries.

contradiction_matrix.name: Contradiction Matrix
contradiction_matrix.description: A grid linking 39 engineering parameters to select the most relevant inventive principles for your contradiction.

inventive_principles.name: 40 Inventive Principles
inventive_principles.description: Apply standard inventive techniques (segmentation, taking out, nesting, etc.) to resolve contradictions.

physical_contradiction.name: Physical Contradiction Separation
physical_contradiction.description: Separate contradictory requirements in time, space, condition, or between parts and whole.

3.name: Physical Contradictions & Systemic Changes
3.description: Significant improvements solving contradictions, often requiring cross-domain knowledge.

su_field.name: Su-Field (Substance-Field) Analysis
su_field.description: Model system components (two substances and a field) to identify interaction failures and improvements.

standard_solutions.name: 76 Standard Solutions
standard_solutions.description: Apply specific rules for improving Su-Field models across 5 classes of solutions.

scientific_effects.name: Scientific Effects Database
scientific_effects.description: Apply principles from physics, chemistry, and geometry to solve problems at a fundamental level.

advanced_trimming.name: Advanced Trimming & Functional Modeling
advanced_trimming.description: Complex, system-level redesign using advanced trimming rules and functional models.

psc_questions.question: Who is facing this problem or will benefit from this solution?
psc_questions.hint: Describe the specific user group, customer segment, or stakeholder experiencing this issue.

psc_questions.question: When and where does this problem occur?
psc_questions.hint: Describe the specific context, environment, or situation in which this problem manifests.

psc_questions.question: What is the root cause of this problem?
psc_questions.hint: Go beyond symptoms — what underlying mechanism, design flaw, or missing capability causes this?

psc_questions.question: What is the impact or consequence of this problem?
psc_questions.hint: Describe the measurable or observable effects — financial, operational, emotional, or social.

psc_questions.question: What solutions or workarounds are currently being used?
psc_questions.hint: What do people do today to cope with or mitigate this problem? Why do these fall short?

psc_questions.question: What constraints or limitations must the solution respect?
psc_questions.hint: Consider cost, regulation, technology availability, user capability, environmental factors.

psc_questions.question: What does an ideal solution look like, and how would you measure success?
psc_questions.hint: Describe the outcome in measurable terms — what changes, for whom, and by how much?

design_thinking_questions.question: Who are your users, and what are their deepest unmet needs?
design_thinking_questions.hint: Think about the human beings at the center of your problem. What do they feel, think, say, and do?

design_thinking_questions.question: What have you observed about how users currently behave around this problem?
design_thinking_questions.hint: What behaviours, workarounds, or frustrations have you noticed in real situations?

design_thinking_questions.question: How would you frame the problem as a 'How Might We' question?
design_thinking_questions.hint: E.g. 'How might we help [user] achieve [goal] without [obstacle]?' Keep it open-ended.

design_thinking_questions.question: What are 3-5 radically different ideas you can think of to address this problem?
design_thinking_questions.hint: No idea is too wild at this stage. Think across industries, scales, and technologies.

design_thinking_questions.question: Which idea seems most promising to prototype, and why?
design_thinking_questions.hint: Consider feasibility, impact, and user desirability. What quick test would validate your key assumption?

design_thinking_questions.question: How would you test this solution with real users?
design_thinking_questions.hint: Describe the simplest experiment that would tell you if you're on the right track.

design_thinking_questions.question: What would success look like after testing, and what feedback would change your direction?
design_thinking_questions.hint: What metrics or signals would confirm the solution works? What would make you pivot?

jtbd_questions.question: What job is the customer trying to get done when they encounter this problem?
jtbd_questions.hint: Think functionally: what progress is the person trying to make in their life or work?

jtbd_questions.question: What are the emotional and social dimensions of this job?
jtbd_questions.hint: How does the user want to feel? How do they want to be perceived by others while doing this job?

jtbd_questions.question: What does the user hire (or fire) products/services to help with this job?
jtbd_questions.hint: What products, services, or behaviours are currently being 'hired' to do this job, even imperfectly?

jtbd_questions.question: What are the key struggles or 'struggling moments' that prompt the switch?
jtbd_questions.hint: What triggers the decision to look for a better solution? Describe a specific situation.

jtbd_questions.question: What forces push users toward a new solution vs. pull them back to the old one?
jtbd_questions.hint: Consider: push (pain with current), pull (attraction to new), anxiety (fear of change), habit (inertia).

jtbd_questions.question: What constraints define the 'outcome metrics' users use to evaluate the job?
jtbd_questions.hint: Speed, accuracy, cost, reliability — what does the user measure to know the job is done well?

jtbd_questions.question: What underserved outcomes define the biggest opportunity for innovation?
jtbd_questions.hint: Which outcome metrics are most important to users but least well served by current solutions?
